input.quote: a. Grant. TrueLink hereby grants to Client a non-exclusive license to use the Interface in the ordinary course of its business of the origination, underwriting, processing and funding of consumer finance receivables in accordance with this Agreement.
input.rationale: The grant in § 2(a) runs to Client alone; neither Client affiliates nor contractors acting on Client's behalf are licensed, and the scope provisions in § 2(b) only permit added sites (Exhibit A) on notice, not added entities, so there is no path to extend use to affiliates or outsourced processors. The transfer position also falls short: § 15 requires the other party's consent for any assignment, with a carve-out only for a financially responsible affiliate and none for a successor in an M&A transaction. The clause therefore fails both limbs of the fallback (affiliates covered on written notice; transferable to a successor). The licence is not expressed as revocable at Vendor's discretion and ends only on termination of the Agreement, so it is not walk-away territory. Minimal redline adds affiliate/contractor coverage to the grant and a successor-transfer carve-out (mutual) to § 15.

proposal.summary: Extend licence to Client affiliates and contractors and permit transfer to a successor.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have extended the licence to cover our affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf, since our origination operations are run partly through affiliated entities and outsourced processors, and added a successor-transfer carve-out to the assignment clause. If preferred, we can accept affiliate coverage on written notice to TrueLink instead.

ops.oldText: TrueLink hereby grants to Client a non-exclusive license to use the Interface
ops.newText: TrueLink hereby grants to Client, its affiliates and its contractors acting on Client's behalf, a non-exclusive license to use the Interface

ops.oldText: except no such approval shall be required for an assignment to a financially responsible affiliate.
ops.newText: except no such approval shall be required for an assignment to a financially responsible affiliate or to a successor in interest in connection with a merger, acquisition, reorganization or sale of all or substantially all of the assigning party's assets.
